claims.claim: the Titanic sank in under three hours (2h40m from collision to foundering)
claims.definition: collision 11:40 PM April 14 1912 to foundering 2:20 AM April 15, per the British Wreck Commissioner's inquiry timeline

claims.claim: lookouts spotted the iceberg at 11:40 PM, about thirty-seven seconds before impact
claims.definition: lookout bell to collision interval as testified by lookouts Fleet and Lee at the British inquiry
claims.authoritative_source: British inquiry testimony (lookouts Fleet and Lee)

claims.claim: the collision breached the first six forward compartments along about three hundred feet of hull
claims.definition: wreck surveys and inquiry damage analysis: bow plates buckled and seams opened across the first six watertight compartments
claims.measured_value: six compartments, approx. 300 ft of hull
claims.authoritative_source: British inquiry damage analysis; wreck survey findings (1985 onward)

claims.claim: the watertight bulkheads rose only to D deck
claims.definition: the transverse bulkheads terminated at D deck; compartments overflowed at the deck line once full
claims.authoritative_source: British inquiry technical findings; Harland & Wolff construction records

claims.claim: design revisions before approval lowered the bulkhead height by roughly ten feet from the earlier drawings
claims.definition: as-built bulkhead tops were about ten feet below the height shown in the earlier design drawing, exchanged for improved accommodation
claims.authoritative_source: design history analyses (Hutchings & de Kerbrech, Titanic: The Ship Magnificent, based on H&W drawings)
claims.notes: phrase kept approximate ('about ten feet') per the design-record precision

claims.claim: of roughly two thousand two hundred aboard, seven hundred and five survived
claims.definition: British inquiry casualty return: 705 survivors of approximately 2,200 people aboard
claims.authoritative_source: British Wreck Commissioner's Inquiry casualty return
claims.notes: 'roughly' retained: exact aboard-count varies by source (2201-2224)
